findings.summary: Mandatory distinct invocations contradict the governing role-separation policy.
findings.rationale: The existing operating model explicitly permits one worker to perform several responsibilities for small changes when deterministic gates preserve separation (docs/development/agent-operating-model.md:152). This Work Item unconditionally requires Reviewer, Hardener, and QA to run as distinct invocations, while only its packet metadata says risk is high. The intended override/scope is undefined, so implementations can either violate the existing contract or silently weaken this Work Item.
findings.direction: Explicitly scope distinct invocations to high-risk/protected Work Items, or amend the operating model as part of this Work Item and define the deterministic exception.

findings.summary: Model-floor enforcement lacks an authoritative classification and unknown-surface rule.
findings.rationale: The acceptance says policy computes a minimum floor from a broad list of affected surfaces, but defines neither the checked-in mapping/precedence nor behavior for unclassified, mixed, or newly introduced surfaces. Without those rules, a Candidate can game classification by avoiding or mislabeling a surface while still satisfying the stated tests.
findings.direction: Specify the authoritative risk-to-floor matrix, protected-surface matching/precedence, and fail-closed behavior for unknown or conflicting surface classifications.

residualRisks: The repository can validate provenance metadata, but genuine host-issued identity/attestation remains externally trusted; the packet acknowledges this limitation.
The four Work Items are sequentially dependent as declared, but 05's host-dependent dogfood acceptance cannot be fully proven by repository tests alone.
